chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ahmad ibn Muhammad said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about fasting in Mecca and Medina while we were traveling. He said, 'It is obligatory (fard).' I said, 'No, but it is voluntary (ta-tawwu'), just as prayer is performed voluntarily.' He said, 'You say, 'Today and tomorrow'?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do not fast.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting in Mecca and Medina for a traveler?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that fasting in Mecca and Medina is an obligatory duty (*fard*) for travelers, distinct from the voluntary fasting permitted elsewhere. The Imam’s follow-up instruction, 'Say today and tomorrow, but do not fast,' indicates that while the obligation remains, the traveler is exempted from actually performing it during those specific days, preserving the status of the act as a duty rather than a mere recommendation. This highlights the unique jurisprudential status of the two holy cities where the traveler's exemption is specific yet the underlying ruling remains binding.
